issues.description: Duplicate "transcriber_error" entry in the message_type tuple
issues.detail: The tuple lists "transcriber_error" twice. Harmless at runtime but it is the kind of sloppy copy-paste that says the author did not read their own diff. Remove it. If you cannot be bothered to read fourteen lines you just wrote, why should the maintainer be?

issues.description: push_error is now called with a positional arg that the old code passed by keyword
issues.detail: Old call sites used error_msg=... as a keyword. The collapsed branch calls push_error(error_msg=f"Error: {error_msg}") which is fine, but the per-type prefixes ("Auth error:", "Quota exceeded:") are gone. Downstream consumers that grep on those prefixes will silently break. Either keep the prefixes or document the contract change in the changelog.

issues.description: Removing the try/except around the async-for loses the disconnect log line entirely
issues.detail: The old code at least logged "WebSocket connection closed: {e}" when the iterator raised. The new _receive_messages just lets the exception bubble. That is the right shape for fixing the infinite loop, but you have also deleted the only breadcrumb operators had. Let it propagate, fine, but log once at warning before re-raising.

This is a bug fix (infinite loop) and a feature (broader error type coverage). They are independent. They should have been two commits with two changelog entries so a future bisect points at the right one. THREE-PATCHES, except it is two.
"\ No newline at end of file" in the diff. Trivial, but every tool that concatenates these files will produce garbage. Add the newline. Match the codebase convention.

issues.description: No test covers either the new error types or the disconnect path
issues.detail: The whole point of the fix is "the process used to hang; now it does not." There is no test asserting that. A small unit test that feeds a disconnect into the iterator and asserts the coroutine returns would have caught the original bug and will catch the regression when somebody re-wraps this in a try/except in six months.

review.summary: The fix is the right shape: the try/except in _receive_messages was swallowing the disconnect and the outer reconnect loop was spinning. Deleting it is correct. The error-type expansion is also fine in principle but sloppy in execution: \"transcriber_error\" listed twice, per-type message prefixes silently dropped, the disconnect log gone with no replacement, and two independent changes shipped as one commit with no test. NEEDS-WORK. Fix the duplicate, restore a single warning log on disconnect, decide explicitly about the prefix contract, add the trailing newline, and add one test for the disconnect path. Then it lands.
